text_fidelity_a: CamelBak Men's Palisade Hike Hydration Pack - Integrated Rain Cover Finally got a chance to take the bag out and put it though it’s paces. We don’t have any camping trips planned for now, but we put a towel and 10 lbs of weight and off we went. He’s 6 feet and skinny for reference. Took it for a thirty minute walk in 90 degrees F and 49% humidity. The pack felt good. The air gap was great, and kept him from overheating. He said the bag sat well and didn’t shift once secured. He is right handed and a lot like my other hiking backpacks, there is only a zipper pocket in the left waist band. This is because you don’t usually reach across to get something in your waist pocket on a hike. The right side is a non zip folded pocket. The rain cover stuffs in a Velcro pocket on the bottom and fits snugly over the entire pack. The large roomy main compartment fits everything I would need for a weekend hike, or a long day hike. Food, camp stove, change of clothing, single man tent, jacket and the large capacity reservoir. There is a hook to put the reservoir on so it doesn’t slip down as you empty the bladder. The bite valve is the standard camelback with shut off (this is important if you have ever been hiking and broken your bite valve and didn’t have time to dig out a spare until base camp.) this is Not a carry your laptop and tootle around town pack. This is a well made solid day/weekend hiker. Yes it would be nice to have a small inner zip pocket, but that’s what carabiners and dry sacks are for. It has a mesh two compartment pocket, and a larger pocket the whole bag length. Water reservoir has its own zippered compartment, and there is one center small zip pocket for quick access item like headlamp. Has a large adjustable mesh pocket on the outside that you can put a helmet, or ground roll. Can’t wait for camping to open up again, I may just steal this from my husband for scout campouts. Product free in exchange for an honest review.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Men's Palisade Hike Hydration Pack - Integrated Rain Cover

text_fidelity_a: Tenzing TZ 720 Lumbar Pack (AP Camo) Let me start by saying that I researched literally dozens of fanny packs before settling on this one. Badlands,Fieldline, LL Bean, ALPS, Allen, Timberhawk, Browning, Cabelas .  .  . you get the picture. I use a fanny pack primarily to run and gun longbeards and to get my archery gear into my hunting locations with a Summit Open Shot Climber on my back. This pack replaces an old fleece 380 cubic inch Fieldline that served me well for many years, but was always just a tad too small.  I can tell you that there are a limited number of packs available that are between what I consider to be too small at 450-500 cubic inches, and for me, too large at over 1000 cubic inches. I don't carry enough gear to require backpack type straps, nor do I want the complications associated with them. Furthermore, many  of the packs that DO tend to fall inside this capacity range  have what I call a "hopper" style zippered opening, which to me makes absolutely no sense. You unzip it and your gear rolls out. I want a top loading pack that retains my gear. If I've just climbed 20' , gotten settled in, unzip my pack and all my gear falls to the ground, well, lets just say I'm not a happy camper. This is a nicely designed pack that met the majority of my parameters developed over 40 years of hunting. This pack, in my opinion, is the perfect size. Enough room for all my gadgets and grub. The side straps "fold" easily and stay "folded" for  easy placement at the back of my platform. Lashing straps top and bottom, check. Plenty of zippered organizing compartments, check. Side strap pockets that actually have some capacity, check.  Oh. . Did I mention this is a great looking pack?  Which leads us to one of my few negatives. The attractive green panels that you see on the front and top of the pack as well as  the entire pack bottom are Dyneema, a super strong synthetic fiber material. Noisy??  Not terribly. Tenzing claims these panels are used for durability, and while I'm fairly certain this pack will indeed outlive my remaining years in the field, they are . . well . . synthetic.  While in my application it means little, if I were using this pack primarily  to stalk or still hunt, it might impact my choice. Get one in your hands and see for yourself. Sizing issue: The reviewer that  mentioned this not cinching up to his 34 waist is spot on. The side straps, at least on the pack i was shipped, are simply too long. I am a 35 waist and can JUST get this pack tight enough. Overall I am extremely happy with the design, build quality, and my Amazon purchase. Nicely done Tenzing.
text_fidelity_b: Tenzing TZ 720 Lumbar Pack (AP Camo)

text_fidelity_a:
Manduka Prolite Yoga and Pilates Premium Mat 4.7mm Thick / Non-Slip, Non-Toxic, Eco-Friendly Certified / Made with Ultra Dense Cushioning for Stability and Support The first time I received this product, it was packaged badly so had some unnatural indents that weren't going away. After a few days, I complained to Amazon and they promptly sent me a new one. The new one was in perfect condition, and I was very excited to try it out. I diligently did the salt scrub that they suggest in the instructions, then gave it a try once the mat had dried.

IT WAS SO SLIPPERY. Like insanely slippery. I do not have sweaty hands or feet, and have never had a problem on cheap yoga mats. I am very disappointed that when I finally decided to invest in an expensive yoga mat, I'm met with all of this unnecessary slipping and sliding. It is slippery to the point where it is actually dangerous to use.

I went online and found that this is a very common problem, especially with the prolite mats. I'm now starting on the arduous journey of trying to 'break in' this mat - a process that people say can take months to a year of intense use. Some people online said that they had more success using some soap as well. I have just recently done a very hard scrub using laundry detergent and salt to try to get rid of what they call a "protective film from the factory" that is causing the slipperiness. This process involves finding an outdoor area, spreading your mat flat, sprinkling salt, then scrubbing the mat using the rough side of a sponge for at least 10 minutes with the laundry detergent or dishwashing soap. I will update this post with how many times I have to do this process to make the mat sticky (hopefully not too many times! I might end up giving up and buying a different brand if it takes too much effort)

I really want this yoga mat to work, so I'm going to sacrifice some time and energy into 'breaking it in' just because so many people have told me how their manduka yoga mat has been life changing for their practice. I am still disappointed that it takes this much time and energy though. For how expensive their mat is, the company should be doing the break-in process for us.

Unless you are willing to put in the time and energy to 'break it in' - don't purchase this product. I have heard the Pro (heavier) yoga mat is not as bad as the prolite with it's break-in process, but I haven't bought the pro so I wouldn't know.

Out of the box, this mat is unusable with how slippery it is.
text_fidelity_b: Manduka Prolite Yoga and Pilates Premium Mat 4.7mm Thick / Non-Slip, Non-Toxic, Eco-Friendly Certified / Made with Ultra Dense Cushioning for Stability and Support

These are difficult to put on and almost impossible to properly tighten. They need an entirely different strap design; something with a clasp or bracket and a friction strap, similar to a backpack, perhaps. Or...who knows. Just about anything would be better than this setup.

text_fidelity_a:
Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire I purchased Campy Shamal 2-way rims a couple years back. I then purchased everything needed to mount and maintain tubeless tires including Fusion 3s. I ride a '12 Specialized S-Works Roubaix and mostly do fast training rides about 3 to 4 days a week with longer rides beyond 60 miles fairly regularly. I weigh out at roughly 185 pounds.

Tubeless and ceramic bearings are somewhat in the same category these days in terms of bikers wondering if this equipment truly makes a difference. Well, I've ridden ceramic bearings in my crank and in my wheels...and YES...it makes a difference...now...I've ridden on tubeless for two riding seasons...and YES...they make a difference. Tubeless is the future...as it is in nearly every vehicle that has wheels from a riding mower to a motorcycle to a car...and mountain bikes. Why it has taken so long with road biking is understandable...change is hard...and manufacturers will go where the money is.

First, let me make this clear...putting the Fusion 3 tires on was a chore...and I mean...a CHORE. It will test your patience. Do NOT succumb to using levers as it will ruin the bead. Google tubeless tire installation for help but even then it will baffle you as to how you're going to get that tire over the rim...but...you will...and the benefits will be worth it.

Second, it takes a few rides to get the tires truly seated. Use an air compressed pump if you've got it...but...I had a "Joe Blow" floor pump that worked fine. I didn't install the sealant until after the second short ride and pump up. You will most likely lose quite a bit of air at first but as the tire seals over time...the air pressure stabilized. I do pump up my tires before every ride but it isn't out of the norm of my former clincher tires.

Third, I've ridden my fusion 3s at 90psi on the front tire and 100psi on the back. The ride is fast & super smooth. A lot of riders think super high psi is better but that is, (arguably for some), not true because at a high psi your tire is actually bumping up and down off the road which drains energy transfer over time. The benefit of running tubeless at lower psi is that the tire remains in more constant contact with the road which...over time...equals better energy transfer...and hence...speed, comfort, and endurance. Also, there is some evidence that without a tube you eliminate friction...I'm honestly not sure about that claim...even so, I can say from experience that I'm not going back to tubed tires...tubeless tires run as advertised.

Fourth, durability...I run typical roads here in Maryland over countless miles...up and down hills...less maintained side roads...and these Fusion 3s can go yet another season. The wear is normal with no unusual issues. I've NOT had one flat tire. I've NOT added more sealant since the first install...which I should've done...but...it hasn't made a difference.

Fifth, the only reservation I have is getting a flat tire but I guess it's a good thing that I'm not as use to dealing with flats like I had for my tubed tires. I have to say it has been a pleasure to not have had one flat for two seasons.

I'd like to try the ATOM version of this tire...and I think I'll get it just for comparison purposes. Not looking forward to the install and my expectation is that they will not fit my riding style, endurance expectations, and my higher weight...even so, I'm a believer in trying anything once...so...we'll see.

All in all...educate yourself but don't be afraid to go tubeless. It is change that we all seem to avoid but I'll never go back now that I've tried it out...and as the biking money goes...tubeless quality and selection will as well. ENJOY!
text_fidelity_b: Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire

The cloth covers for the rear saddles make sliding your kayak up easy and the straps, guylines and hooks are good quality. I used this product when I picked up my new fishing kayak and drove 90 miles with it home.

Now to the "for some kayaks" part. The saddles pivot and fold in or out to adjust to various kayak hull diameters. For a traditional kayak or canoe hull this would work really well and automatically center the boat in the saddles. However I have a Wilderness Systems Radar 135 fishing kayak. The hull is a fairly complex shape with the sides being almost square and continuing underneath into a pontoon section on both sides and a fairly flat bottom in the middle. The prow is pointed like a normal, but flattens out after about 2 feet. All these weird shapes combine to make it difficult to center the boat on the saddles and trying to adjust the boat once on the saddles is difficult. Will be looking for an alternative rack.

It's a good product, unfortunately it just won't work very well for the type of kayak I have. Anybody in the market for a used once kayak rack? :P

What a difference! I will never ever ever wear non-flatlands goggles again. I guarantee if you try each on, you will wonder why they even make curved lens goggles!

Goggles are made of a substance that does not lend itself to being curved. Every single thing is blurred. Above or below water. You put a flat lens pair on and boom! Every single thing is clear above and below water.

It’s such a pleasure. It’s like wiping grease away from a window and seeing clearly again. I thought I’d have issues with being near sighted… But of course water magnifies and with flat lenses, nothing was an issue.

All thanks to reading one of many reviews when trying to get to the bottom of what swim goggles on Amazon are great.

Ozark Trail 12 Can Cooler Bag Insulated Tote Hot/Cold Thermal, Expandable Top, Hard Plastic Liner, Shoulder Strap, for Lunch Work School Camping, Blue Last week my former cooler without the Ozark Trail logo, but which was actually an Ozark Trail unfortunately met a tragic demise, being dragged behind Bubba the 4 wheeler. Operator error, actually. But I didn't come here to assess blame. No. I came here to praise the Ozark Trail 12 Can Expandable Top Soft-sided Cooler.
I had had the previous cooler for years and years and years. Could not tear it up. Took Bubba to do that. So within an hour of burying the last one I came here to see if the thing still existed. I found many similar coolers, the most expensive costing $300. At that price it should have come with a complimentary built in solar refrigerator. Alas, it did not. Just an ordinary cooler with a very recognizable trendy logo.
After a time I saw that indeed the son of my cooler DID exist in the form of the Ozark Trail 12 Can Expandable Top Soft-sided Cooler. I pounced.
This early morning before daylight (late summer) it sits just beyond this room stuffed with ice and water for another excursion to the jungles, less Bubba this time. To practicalities: I don't do cans. I do bottled water. It will hold 4 28oz bottles and still have enough room to ice it all down very well indeed. It's sort of like one of those motel ice buckets with a soft cover around it. The ice will last all day, out of the sun. There is indeed a front pouch, which will hold a couple of sammiges, etc. The top comfortably holds a lunch bag and will keep it semi-cold. As you no doubt noted in the sparse description provided above, there is a middle zipper so that the whole top can be expanded a notch if you have more than one sammige. You won't find this on any other cooler, and this alone makes it a wise purchase.
The Ozark Trail 12 Can Expandable Top Soft-sided Cooler is about the cheapest one around...(Even the sales pitch above is sort of take it or leave it cheap) and the most versatile. You can't kill the thing unless you drag it behind an ATV, car, or possibly a boat. Unless you demand Goochie Brand sneakers to go to the opera, you'll be more than pleased with this excellent cooler. Fact. And yes, I have seen the crappy reviews. I have no idea.
I got mine. Get yours. But don't get the last one. Bubba stays hungry.
text_fidelity_b: Ozark Trail 12 Can Cooler Bag Insulated Tote Hot/Cold Thermal, Expandable Top, Hard Plastic Liner, Shoulder Strap, for Lunch Work School Camping, Blue

text_fidelity_a: Cornilleau Sport 500M Outdoor Table Tennis Table The assembly instructions were adequate but could have been better with pictures and just a bit of explanation. Assembly took two of us a pretty leisurely two hours. In terms of quality, I was a bit disappointed with the amount of structural plastic and the complete lack of flat washers that would likely allow the hinged portions to function and wear better. Time will tell how the table wears. It does appear solid and the folding/unfolding works very well. I am a novice player, but have a number of advanced and tournament players at my office whose advice I sought before purchase. We have a quality table at work and so far, I can't tell the difference in the bounce or feel of the table. YMMV. If you intend to unfold, use, fold, move the table both inside and outside on a variety of surfaces, I think this table will be a good choice. Cornilleau would certainly be wise to team with a shipper who would offer white glove delivery and assembly service. I would have used it.
text_fidelity_b: Cornilleau Sport 500M Outdoor Table Tennis Table

text_fidelity_a:
MOON LENCE Outdoor Ultralight Portable Folding Chairs with Carry Bag Heavy Duty 242lbs Capacity Camping Folding Chairs Beach Chairs I've been wanting an ultralight chair since my buddy bought a mantis last year. A year ago these chairs were $150. Amazing how quickly a good idea disseminates.

Is it quite as nice in the fit/finish as the expensive ones? nope. But so far, it's got some great design features and doesn't feel rickety at all.

Goes together easily, every tube is elasticized to the hole. If the elastic ever breaks, you can still assemble it easily, so don't sweat that.

You assemble it by first putting the bottom of the chair on the posts (after you get all the posts stuck together) and then in the pockets where the upper poles mount are... two finger rings! absolutely genius! they make stretching the fabric tightly enough to fit the poles a breeze. Great little idea.

It's small enough to fit into a backpack but holds my 6'3, 180lb butt so comfortably. It's a good seating position, you can recline in it or sit hunched forward for eating, so the ergos are spot on. Very balanced to sit in, doesn't feel like you'll fall at all. Sure, it's a couple pounds, but when you get to camp and your friends are all sitting on a cold, wet log trying to find the good spot around the fire, you'll be lounging in comfort.
text_fidelity_b: MOON LENCE Outdoor Ultralight Portable Folding Chairs with Carry Bag Heavy Duty 242lbs Capacity Camping Folding Chairs Beach Chairs

I'm a bit different than most folks because I actually sleep on a 20" tall queen size air mattress every night and have done so for the past two years. I mention this because of the way I use a pillow when sleeping - it is molded, puffed out and reformed several times during the night.  That just can't happen with this air pillow.  For me, it serves more as a back prop for sitting up and reading on the bed.  Nice and firm, it gives me back support while sitting up in bed.  It does store well in the very small case it comes in and that's perfect!  As I have gotten older and had to move when I didn't really want to but circumstances made me, I have become addicted to "nomadic furniture" that is easier to move than traditional furniture.  An air pillow does fit within my parameters of small and packable!  Same with my bed - not quite a small, but certainly nothing like lugging around a heavy, floppy queen size mattress and box springs!  So, all in all, I am pleased with this air pillow at least for what I will use it for.

text_fidelity_a:
Fox Outdoor Products Mission Ready Drop Leg Holster I wanted to try a drop leg holster for some time and came across this model in desert camo through another vendor. For the price, and because I had heard good things about Fox, I decided to take advantage of the reduced price and see how good (or bad) this holster really is.

The first day, after strapping it on and making all the adjustments I could, I carried around a mini ball peen hammer just to try to get used to it. Why did I choose a hammer? While I am CCW licensed, Florida does not currently allow "open carry". So I had to put something of measurable weight in the holster without alarming the neighbors or anyone driving by on our street. I could imagine someone seeing me with a drop leg holster and calling our local law enforcement, not knowing that their was no gun in the holster -- but assuming there was.Yes, the weight of the hammer head made the holster cant backwards, so I switched to a rubber mallet. This provided a much better balance.

Then I switched to a Glock 23 and a Springfield XD-45 MOD 2 and alternately carried both around inside our home, After trying my darndest to get it to fit properly, I came to the following conclusions:

1. This is a cool looking and well constructed rig. The desert camo design is well done, the material is light and flexible, and the various
clips, belts and fasteners work like they should.
2 The holster accommodated both the Springfield and Glock perfectly and the strap easily fastened over the gun butt.
3. It is very light and designed to fit comfortably against your thigh.
4. And of course it easily carries a lighter weight weapon like a Kahr PM9 and a Glock 42. In fact the smaller and lighter pistols eliminate
the bounding around explained below. But who wants to carry a "pocket pistol" in a drop leg holster?

But, and this is a "big but" for me, the single strap that fastens the holster around your thigh just couldn't keep the holster secure and steady. It bounced while walking and really moved around when running (even at my slow pace). I tightened the thigh strap so that over 14" of strap was outside the buckle, but it just never felt secure. No one wants that feeling -- you want your gun to be right where it's supposed to be -- all of the time.

This holster really needs two improvements: 1. It needs a second strap to go around the thigh, one high and one low. 2. It also needs more vertical adjustment so that it can be carried a bit higher on your belt. Both of these changes would result in a better fit and should eliminate excess movement.
text_fidelity_b: Fox Outdoor Products Mission Ready Drop Leg Holster

Hand Warmers Rechargeable, 2 Pack Electric Magnetic Portable Hand Warmer,Reusable 10000mAh Power Bank, 360° Heating & Max 15Hrs Warmth Time, 3 Levels Temp, Women, Men I own four other hand warmers, all of them one-piece batteries. At a first glance, this hand warmer looks very similar, but you soon realize it has double the number of ports and buttons of a typical hand warmer. And that’s because this one warmer is actually two halves attached magnetically. You can use it as a single unit, with both sides heating, or you can split it into two independent halves and put each half in a different hand or pocket, or use one half as a warmer and the other half to charge your phone. The caveat is that the external, rounded part of each half is the only one that heats. The internal, flat part that can attach to the other half magnetically does not produce heat. I don’t think that’s a downside. If you are holding one of the halves of the warmer in the palm of your hand, the heating side perfectly fits your palm, and the flat side is only covered by your fingertips, so any heat would be wasted anyway.

Each half warmer has a 5000mAh battery, so in theory you have a combined 10000mAh.

Bottomline: I like the concept of two independent batteries that are shaped so they can also function as a single unit. That concept distinguishes this warmer from the other four I own.
text_fidelity_b: Hand Warmers Rechargeable, 2 Pack Electric Magnetic Portable Hand Warmer,Reusable 10000mAh Power Bank, 360° Heating & Max 15Hrs Warmth Time, 3 Levels Temp, Women, Men

text_fidelity_a:
NEOMEN Snore Stopper, Anti Snoring Devices, Advanced Snoring Solution to Ease Breathing and Snoring The first thing I did after washing this bottle was to fill it up with spring water and put it in the refrigerator for three weeks. When I finally took it out to taste the water, it was just as pure and tasteless as when I poured it in. And that's a good thing. No one likes to drink water that tastes like metal. I originally bought this bottle because of the uniformly good reviews and the advantages i perceived of using it in a hot climate.

I am just starting to ride a road bike at age 64 because I'd like to get regular exercise again without further damaging my joints. The Hydro Flask provides me with the necessary hydration during rides in ninety degree plus weather. It holds enough water to keep me out of trouble for two hours and keeps it cold. The flask is built like a tank and fits perfectly in my tube cage. It should be perfect for short jaunts and the different colors available allows you to match it to your bike frame.

If I progress to riding with the "A" riders eventually, I could see the need for a Camelback system. But for now, the Hydro Flask gives me all I need. That and the dream of being an "A" rider.
text_fidelity_b: NEOMEN Snore Stopper, Anti Snoring Devices, Advanced Snoring Solution to Ease Breathing and Snoring

text_fidelity_a:
Exerpeutic 400XL Folding Recumbent Exercise Bike Ordered this from Amazon December 20, 2015 and it was delivered the following Sunday. I assembled the bike a few hours after it arrived without troubles.

For some reason there is a full page parts diagram of the entire bike that is shown prior to the assembly instructions. The diagram made things look way more complicated than they turned out to be. Turns out (most) of the hardware is already in place and just needs to be aligned and tightened (with the included tools).

I assembled this on my own and most people should be able to do just like I did. One note on assembly though: the main part of this is the bulk of the total weight of the entire bike. It's a bit on the heavy side so if lifting heavy objects is hard or risky for you you should seek out some help.

The pedals went on super quick and easy. They were clearly marked 'L' and 'R' and the instructions made sure there were clear on which way the bolts should be threaded.

I've since put 320 miles on the odometer on this, so, about 14.5 miles a day. I haven't noticed any mechanical problems or glaring defects. I enjoy the fact the the seat is adjustable to some degree and the adjustable tension works surprisingly well.

My reason for giving only four stars is because of the seat. It is very hard and after a while it causes pain. I'm going to get a nice cover for it and hopefully that will help some with that.

Other than that, this is a great bike for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Exerpeutic 400XL Folding Recumbent Exercise Bike

Opened it and cleaned it out and oiled it...no problems now. I caution about removing the bail covers. A spring and rod can come out and it took some doing to get it back in. I had to get the schematic from Shimano. The easiest way to re-assemble is to put the rod and spring in its place at the rear of the compartment replace the chrome cover and then insert the spring shaft into the bail housing in the hole provided. Then put the bail in place and put in the screw. Really no big deal but others not mechanically inclined may want to just send it off to have it completely cleaned.

This reel casts a mile due to the aero line wrap system that prevents line from becoming entrapped under other line. The retrieve and reeling is smooth as butter. The knob has bearing so there is no dragging whatsoever.

I fish this reel in salt and fresh water and have had no issues due to saltwater use. It is certified by Shimano to be saltwater safe.
I will be ordering my second one soon.

Empower Admittedly, it may seem too early for me to review the Empower Kettlebell & DVD I received yesterday. However, based on past workout purchases, and experiences, I believe this one's a keeper. I went for the 10-pound Kettlebell, and feel this is a good choice. It comes with a DVD with three levels of workouts, starting with one for beginners such as myself. It also includes warmup and cool-down routines, which are highly recommended before and after each workout respectively.

I started today, and after just one workout, I can already feel my core, leg, and arm muscles reacting to workout #1. While I have a little trouble with the 10-pound weight for some of the curl exercises, I modify the exercises to accommodate my lack of strength, and believe the 10-pound bell was a good choice because it allows me more room to grow -- which will be marked by my eliminating the need for modifications before moving on to the second workout.

In facing my 61st birthday, I'm active, and want to stay that way. This is why I'm determined to get in the best shape of my life (even in my early years, I've never been big on exercise). I started a month ago by purchasing a pair of Skecher Shape-ups, and taking brisk walks with my dogs each morning. To break the monotony, I purchased an MP3 player, and download books from the library. The time flies by!

I added resistance weeks ago with a trip to the gym, intent on going and working out every other day. Then reality hit. It took too long to get dressed, get my walk in, and then go to the gym, work out, come home and clean up. My mornings were shot. So I needed another way to achieve my goal.

A friend told me about Kettlebells. Now, after just one short Kettlebell workout, I've accomplished as much as when using several machines at the gym. The best part is it's fast. I can hop out of bed, and get it done quickly.

Based on numerous past workout experiences and money wasted on a variety of machines and other programs and gimmicks, I'm convinced this is what I've been searching for. I'd recommend it to anyone thinking of starting to get in shape, and wanting fast results. If you're new to working with weights, which I am not, you might want to start with the Empower 5-Pound KettleBell with DVD, and then work your way up to heavier Kettlebells. [[ASIN:B001O0EG7S Empower 10-Pound KettleBell with DVD]]

text_fidelity_a:
Condor Tool & Knife, TRT (Tactical Rescue Tomahawk), Paracord Wrapped Handle with Sheath I own several Condor sharp-edged tools and have never been disappointed in any of them. My collection of Hatchet/Tomahawk/Breaching Tools includes cheap models from United Cutlery to expensive tools from RMJ Tactical and the Busse family. You can break the cheaper ones with little effort so it's important to distinguish between "pretty or tacticool" and durable/useful. If you want an all-purpose tactical rescue tool this $50.00 Condor TRT is probably the cheapest one that I would trust to perform consistently in a tough environment.

It came out of the box razor sharp -- as in sharp enough to slice a piece of paper. There is a nice sheath that fits over the head but you'll need to stretch it and work it to snap the first time. The sheath also has a belt loop on it for side carry. Now why would I give it four stars instead of five? First off the paracord wrapped handle is slippery. You can remedy that with some sandpaper and create a grip that you are comfortable with.

But the biggest problem is in the weight distribution. This is a full tang hawk with a hollow steel handle and the head is offset to one side. Strange construction that but probably an attempt at keeping this TRT hawk from being too heavy. The strength and durability of this tool is not a concern but the strange (lack of) balance is. Shifting more weight to the head would balance it more properly and make the damage inflicted by the downward strike all the more devastating.

All-in-all though this $50.00 Condor TRT is probably worth twice as much as it costs. Just be aware that it has some drawbacks that might affect your performance with it. If things get too bad you can simply turn it upside down and grip it just below the blade to deliver a heavy handled blow.
text_fidelity_b: Condor Tool & Knife, TRT (Tactical Rescue Tomahawk), Paracord Wrapped Handle with Sheath

FVSA Rechargeable Hand Warmer - Christmas Stocking Stuffers Gifts, 7 Changing Colors Lights Electric Hand Warmers 10000Mah, (13-18 Hours) Portable USB Reusable, Winter Gifts for Men & Women This hand warmer comes with a short micro cord for charging. AC power adapter not included. It also comes with a carrying strap and a velour pouch. It’s in a nice box, which makes it very easy to wrap, if you’re giving it as a gift.

There are a lot of very similar hand warmers being sold on Amazon right now by Chinese companies. The one difference with this one is the light going around the edge. They call it “breathing lights”, for some unknown reason. First of all, you can choose to have the light on or not. Second, you can either have it as one color. . . or. .it will change between colors.

You have to press the on/off button for three-seconds to turn the hand warmer on. . . or. . .off. Then you press it quickly to change between the three heat levels. The one thing I don’t like about this hand warmer is the fact that the power / heat level button is on the side. If the hand warmer is in your pocket, it’s very easy to simply tap it accidentally and the heat level will change without your knowing.

Made in China.

text_fidelity_a:
Citadel Black Zombie Apocalypse Survival Kit - Multi-Tool, Fire Starter, Keyring, Zombie Permit, Stickers, and More I am severely disappointed in this product. All the reviews make it out to be something it most certainly is not. This is just a novelty kit with about $5 work of product (if that). Neat concept, poor execution. If you're looking for a survival kit with products that will actually help you survive something in real life...THIS IS NOT IT. Even as a themed novelty kit, this is junk. Save your money.

The most useful items are the anti-bacterial goop and the bandaids.

The card multi-tool could be useful, but ALL the edges are sharp and can easily break skin.

The "tactical knife" is a card-knife that can neither be properly locked open or properly locked closed. It struggled with cutting the plastic this survival kit came wrapped in.

The dust mask is unfinished on the edges. It can easily become unraveled and had lots of loose ends fresh out of the package.

There was a tea candle. Yep.

Compass did not point North. Ever.

Glow sticks were not bright enough to illuminate the desk they were lying right on.

The fire starter is a joke. Don't get me wrong..With some skill it can be used, but it is absolute junk. I broke the metal bar after a few practice tries.

Overall, if I hadn't had a gift card to waste, I would have returned the item for a refund. Even my son who is all about zombie survival thought it was junk.
text_fidelity_b: Citadel Black Zombie Apocalypse Survival Kit - Multi-Tool, Fire Starter, Keyring, Zombie Permit, Stickers, and More

text_fidelity_a:
Masters Macrolight Adjustable Length Bi-Material Carbon Aluminum Trekking Poles (Black, 60-135-cm) I loved how light they are. These are really well made poles, but I returned them unused. With no gloves on, I couldn't set the length, lock in place and lean on them to simulate a fall without them slipping. And no way could I lock them with gloves on. This is not a knock on the manufacturer. Twist lock mechanisms are bound to fail over time. These would probably be excellent in the summer when you are not wearing gloves. The foam handles are firm get giving. Not sure how absorbent the handles are.

The final thing I learned, which I'll try to confirm with other carbon poles, is that there is significant vibration when you smack a pole down (I was simulating on carpet). Man, these poles resonate! You feel it in your hands. This might not be a bad thing. For carbon fiber bicycles, the give in the material creates a dampening effect. This could be a great alternative to an active shock absorbing mechanism. We'll see...

UPDATE 02/12/2014
I bought Leki carbon poles and went did 4k+ vertical, 2k+ in snow. Yes, you want carbon. The lighter the better! I'm new to snowshoeing, so I fell a few times. They took the bend. The give in the poles is the right amount of dampening for me. Perfect.

text_fidelity_a:
Nail Drills for Acrylic Nails Professional Electric Nail File, RenoJ Portable Electric Nail Drill Efile Nail Filer Electric (Pink) This is a great little nail drill with lots of positives, but there's still room for improvement. This is basically a miniature Dremel tool for fingernails.

PROS:
• Very quiet.
• USB cord is lighter than electrical cord.
• Nice range of speeds from slow to fast.
• Speeds are variable so you're not stuck with just a few predetermined speeds.
• Can reverse the spin direction.
• Came with more accessories than you'll ever need (and they're in really cute little containers).

NEUTRALS:
• Easy to hold, but still a little bulky. Would be better if it was smaller: thinner and shorter.
• Nice smooth metal case, but it easily slips when holding it – I added a gel pencil grip which stopped the slipping problem.

CONS:
• Must be plugged in to use – it would be great if it had a rechargeable battery.
• Switches for on/off, direction, and speed are inconveniently placed – Instead of being on the tool itself, they're on the cord, about a foot away from the tool. You have to reach down the cord for each adjustment. They move around as the cord moves.
• The drill rolls – Anytime you put it down, it rolls away. The cord can help limit the rolling, but when it's unplugged, there is nothing to stop it from rolling off the table. I put a gel pencil grip on the drill to help stop this.
• The nail bits are kept in two mismatched plastic containers with different lengths, widths, and thicknesses. When combined with the bag for the sanding bands, you end up needing a container to hold all the containers! It would be better if at least the nail bits were all in one, single container.

Overall, this is a good little tool for filing nails. Hopefully, newer versions will be even better.
text_fidelity_b: Nail Drills for Acrylic Nails Professional Electric Nail File, RenoJ Portable Electric Nail Drill Efile Nail Filer Electric (Pink)

Mainly, I would use the Havalon razors to get started, but then use the heavy blade for larger areas. I would then switch back to the Havalon for the finer cuts. Sometimes the razor is just too sharp for my preference. For this reason, I held off on purchasing one, but used my friends somewhat regularly on hunting trips.

Right after I heard that the double-bladed version was out, I jumped on it. This thing is exactly what I wanted out of a skinning knife. I can switch between the razor and the heavier blade quickly and don't have to keep track of 2 knives. It's not very large and not even that heavy. Given all that and the price, I must say that I am pretty happy with it. I did my first deer with this knife shortly after I purchased it and am really happy with it.

I know everyone has their preference on knives when it comes to skinning, but this thing is perfect for my needs and I'm very happy with it.
text_fidelity_b: Havalon Titan Jim Shockey Signature Series

There is also a protective foam over the water tube from the bag to the end of the tube. The mouthpiece has a cap cover which stays attached with a piece of plastic so you can't drop the cover. Overall I think it is a great water backpack with plenty of room for a day hike.

text_fidelity_a:
PRETTYGAGA Plus Holds Cell Phone，Outdoor Tactical， Messenger Bag， Military Trekking As a woman who wants to enjoy the concealed carry option but doesn’t want to carry an extra purse for cell phone, cash, etc., I have to say this little case takes care of it all. It has so much functionality that I almost don’t know where to start.

Laying flat and without anything in it, this very durable and well-made nylon case measures about 7-1/2” wide x 9-1/2” tall. That also includes a gusset which, when extended, accommodates a pretty good sized gun. Almost all the seams are double-stitched, and an outer strong and durable bungee style closure keeps the pockets on the outer side of the purse secure. In addition to the larger inner pocket where you can stash your weapon (or if not a weapon will hold quite a bit of other things), there is also a front outer pocket that is perfect for a cell phone. My Galaxy J7 fits great. Another great feature is you have the option of carrying this case like a purse with the removable strap, or you can remove the strap and wear on your belt.

There is a wide band of Velcro in the front of the case which, when opened reveals 10 card slots (including 1 clear for I.D.), a zippered pocket which is perfect size for cash bills, and a pocket behind each set of card slots where you can store coupons, receipts, etc. **I do want to note that while the zipper pouch is great for bills, it may not be great for loose change because if you unzipper the bill slot with the case in upright/vertical position which it would be if you are wearing it, and loose change may fall out. There is also a zipper pocket right at the very top of the purse actually at the top of the front flap. Unzip that and you’ll find a great little pocket for an extra magazine (or 2-3 depending on the size). It could also be a good pocket to hold your keys. On the back side of this pouch there is another zipper compartment that can easily hold a larger size cell phone or extra ammo mags or even your gun depending on the size.

Overall, this is a great case that can be used by men or women, and I can’t find anything that I don’t like about it. It’s a keeper!
text_fidelity_b: PRETTYGAGA Plus Holds Cell Phone，Outdoor Tactical， Messenger Bag， Military Trekking

Any device that counts waving and typing as step counts is too sensitive, therefore inaccurate and useless. Why spend the money only to be one of the cool kids!?!?)

I went into this with a bit of a negative attitude. But given the price even if all it did was tell time I'd be content. Wow! It is good to be wrong!! I have worn this constantly for 2 months resulting in the following review.

Once it paired with my Samsung Galaxy I was impressed with the size and brightness of the clock display. Then came the fun stuff. Setting up for local weather; current, tomorrow, and next day and it's always accurate.

Caller ID, texts, email and incoming calls notifications are a higher intensity vibration than others I've tried. I have always felt the Mi Band 3 vibration regardless of what I'm doing. I really like this while my phone is muted so I remember to check it later. I can also read the shorter messages if my phone is out of reach.

I can't vouch for degree of waterproofing but it's certainly shower and dish washing proof which is good since the Xiaomi Mi Band is lightweight and very comfortable so I often forget I'm wearing it.

I like that I can set it when I go to the gym and get a reading on steps, distance, heart rate, etc. This becomes a subset of the daily activity record.

The sedentary reminder is helpful when I'm ‘in the zone’ while working on a project. I'm not convinced the heart rate is accurate but I suspect it's fairly close for those if us not needing a medical reason to monitor our heart. I don't believe much of anything the Sleep Monitor says but then I don't care about that either.

The battery life is at least 2 weeks. I've only charged mine 3 times in 2 months.

Nothing is perfect, including this Mi Band 3. Navigating through the myriad of settings can be frustrating. There is definitely a learning curve when trying to figure out how to see a specific option : Swipe up? Swipe down? Swipe to the side? Which side?

The other issue is when it changes to military time or suddenly jumps an hour or two ahead/behind for no reason. It took me awhile to find the fix for these problems. Shut down Bluetooth and turn off phone for a minute or two. Turn phone back on, turn on Bluetooth and after about a minute everything should go back to the way you had it originally. I've only had each of these problems happen once.

I am very impressed with the Mi Band 3. And the options can't be beat, especially for the price. This would be a good starter fitness band for a kid or someone just wanting to see if a fitness band is useful to have.
text_fidelity_b: Xiaomi Fitness Tracker, Mi Band 3 Heart Rate Monitor Activity Tracker Watch 50M Waterproof Smart Bracelet 0.78 OLED Display Weather Forecast Wristband Pedometer Calories Burned Sleep Monitor Black

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Company Signature Instant Cabin 10 Person Classic Tent, Black/Grey UPDATE Feb 2018: We've used this tent a lot in the last couple years. I started out really liking it except for a few little things. But now, the more I use it, the more I hate it. The primary cause of that is the door zippers. They are a major pain to zip and unzip, constantly getting stuck. It just ruins the whole peacefulness of camping when you're fighting a stupid zipper. Next is the bag. One of the seams has completely ripped making the bag almost useless, and the tent really needs a bag, even if it's flimsy crappy quality like what it comes with. Dropping from 4 to 3 stars.

Have used this tent 3 times now for camping. Overall, we really like the tent, but there are a few cons...

1. This is a big footprint - 10' x 14'. Where we camp - in the Sierra's mostly - it's not always easy to find that big of a spot that is level. And you DO want it level. For one, you need to sleep on level ground. Two, the legs won't adjust very well to unlevel ground which makes the tent lean and be unstable.

2. Thought we would like the idea of the "hinged" door, but honestly it's just a pain. It comes with 2 fiberglass poles that fit into hard plastic cups in the door. The poles have rubberized tips to keep them from poking through the cups, but they inevitable get stuck in the cups and pull off the poles. Then they poke holes into the cups making the whole system useless. The long pole that goes around the rim is a real pain to bend into position. Then, once the whole thing is installed, the door doesn't fit well when closed. Kinda hangs at a wierd angle leaving gaps in the doorway so that bugs and critters can get in. So basically we ditched the poles and just use the door like a regular tent and zip/unzip whenever we go in or out. Leading to the next issue...

3. The zippers are not high quality and frequently get jammed up. Not fun anytime, but especially not in the middle of the night.

4. The storage bag, which we think is pretty essential, is junk. Very thin and flimsy material with lousy stitching. Ours split a seam on the first repacking. The material is so thin that it's probably useless to try and restitch it. We'll probably re-purpose one of our old military duffel bags as a new bag. Not ideal.

5. Kinda nitpicky, but there aren't any loops or hooks for hanging lanterns or anything else. Seems like an oversight.

6. Sloping sides makes it awkward to move around a queen mattress it you have it in the middle. Fortunately, there's two doors, one on each end.

What we like about it:

1. Super easy to set up and tear down. My wife and I can have this up/down in about 5 minutes, and I can do it myself easily. Just take a little time and make sure the legs are positioned correctly. There is no need to force anything, so if you're trying to force something, you're doing it wrong. However, there is no indication on the tent when folded that indicates where the main door is. When you've set it up once - use a sharpie on the top pole hub to indicate the direction of the front door so you can point it in that direction when setting it up. Again, it helps to have level ground so the legs don't get kinked in any weird directions. Watch setup videos a few times so you have it imprinted what it should look like.

2. The space is great. Just right for the two of us! We have plenty of room for a queen air mattress and separate spaces for each of our stuff. So far, we haven't found a big enough flat spot to give us flexibility in where we put the mattress (except in the backyard), so we haven't settled on the ideal mattress placement.

3. Love the top screen for star gazing in bed and all the windows.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Company Signature Instant Cabin 10 Person Classic Tent, Black/Grey

text_fidelity_a:
Sit N Cycle sitNcycle SNC2 Dorothy Hamill Deluxe XL Low Resistance Exercise Bike It's not perfect, but it does the job. We liked it enough that we bought two, His and Hers.

Here's some hints on assembly:
1. Open the box from the top, using the 'this side up' arrrow as your guide. They have a clever trick to use the styrofoam packing as a frame to hold the bike during assembly, so you need to start out with the right relationship. At this point, you should Read The ....Friendly...Manual before you go off doing stuff.
2. The styrofoam is fragile. Be careful when you lift it off and put the bike body on it.
3. I found that it's more comfortable to work on the bottom assembly if you stack a couple of boards or bricks under the base end.
4. The first step has you trying to attach the base by screwing in four bolts and washers through four access holes in the plastic bottom. It's hard to see and hard to manipulate and the washers keep falling off. I solved that by removing the two middle pan head screws so that I could pull out the plastic bottom (which appears to be there just to keep out armadillos) and reach in to stabilize the screws as I put them in. If you wanted to, you could remove all five pan heads and not worry about bending the plastic bottom. When you are done, replace the pan head screws, and finish attaching the bottom cover by screwing in the final two pan heads next to the wheels.

It pedals very smoothly, and you feel like you are riding a unicycle. We have not had the pedal problems other have, but we don't use it that intensively. Like many other exercise bikes, it tones your legs, not your arms or upper body. You could carry weights in your hands, or you could just give up on that and read a book while you bike.
text_fidelity_b: Sit N Cycle sitNcycle SNC2 Dorothy Hamill Deluxe XL Low Resistance Exercise Bike
